newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian rights group blasts PLO, Israel.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian rights group blasts PLO, Israel.

text.p: Palestinian rights activists on Thursday accused the Palestinian Authority of systematic violations of human rights despite some improvements in the behaviour of some security forces.

The Palestinian Society for the Protection of Human Rights and the Environment (LAW) in its annual report on the West Bank and Gaza Strip also blasted Israel for arbitrary arrests of Palestinians, land confiscation, and torture.

The report came two weeks after a Palestinian inmate named Yousef al-Baba died in an Authority lockup allegedly from torture. The Palestinian Authority has detained two senior officials for questioning in Baba's death.
"The Palestinian Authority continues to carry out arbitrary arrests and employs torture against detainees," LAW director Khader Shqairat told a news conference in Jerusalem.
"These violations indicate that they are part of a systematic policy carried out by the security forces."

Iyad al-Sarraj, a human rights campaigner jailed in the past for criticising the Palestinian Authority, told the news conference Baba's death indicated violations were continuing despite some improvements.

"Despite the improvements that came in the behaviour of the Palestinian Authority in the last months of 1996, which is quite noticeable in the police and the Preventive Security Service, there are many violations that spread terror, the latest of which was the death of Baba in Nablus," Sarraj said.
Human rights organisations say 12 Palestinians have died under torture since the PLO took over self-rule in most of the West Bank and Gaza in 1994.
Sarraj and Shqairat also slammed Israeli military authorities.
"The Israeli occupation continues and its violations remain," Shqairat said. Israel has handed parts of the West Bank and most of Gaza to Palestinian rule in interim peace deals.
"Israel continues to confiscate land, destroy houses, carry out arbitrary arrests and revoke residency cards of (Jerusalem) Palestinians," he said.
